messages:
Marta K: Thinking about ownership handoff for billing when events arrive late. Two proposals: short leases vs per-(tenant,fingerprint) counters. Tradeoffs?
Alex D: Leases feel simpler conceptually but worry about per-token state explosion and GC.
Devon R: Counters reduce ephemeral lease state but add hot-key leader complexity. We can shard counters by tenant-prefix.
Samir: Independent of approach: keep append-only raw_events for audit/backfills; fast-path uses compacted claim rows.
Chris P: Backfills bypass leases; need reconciliation job to detect duplicates and emit compensating credits.
Marta K: Suggest default lease 5m, tenant-configurable. For counters, only accept strictly increasing seq; out-of-order go to audit.
Alex D: Metrics: lease_conflict_rate or claim_counter_skips, audit_reconcile_lag. Alert thresholds TBD.
Devon R: Pseudocode for finalizer CAS should be in RFC. Also store provenance (last_offset, source, backfill_id) on claim row.
Samir: Backfill plan: ingest as audit-only with backfill_id tag, run dry-run, then materialize claims if safe.
Chris P: Runbook: on spike in conflicts -> pause auto-apply, run audit-reflow for affected tenants, compute compensations, resume.
infra-bot: finalizer-service v2 deployed to staging :white_check_mark:
Marta K: I'll write RFC covering handshake protocol, envelope schema v2, compact vs audit paths, backfill & reconciliation, GC, metrics, and migration steps. Reviewers: @Alex D, @Devon R. :thumbsup:
